Primary proposition.statement="Babin–Ilyin–Titi primary results in their normalized mean-zero homogeneous spaces on R/(2 pi Z): write U_t=U U_x+U_xxx, Uhat(k)=exp(-it k^3) z_k(t), so z'_k=(ik/2) sum_{k1+k2=k}exp(3it k k1 k2)z_{k1}z_{k2}. A weak solution satisfies this integrated equation at every nonzero k. For every s>=0, B0>=0, horizon b>0 and initial z0 in dot H^s with ||z0||_2<=B0, the Galerkin equations z'_k=Pi_m[(ik/2) sum_{k1+k2=k} exp(3it k k1 k2)(Pi_m z)_{k1}(Pi_m z)_{k2}], z(0)=z0, have a bound sup_{[0,b]}||z^(m)||_{dot H^s}<=K_s(b,B0,||z0||_{dot H^s}), uniformly in m; the proof supplies a bound uniform when the indicated initial norm is bounded. For s>0 and 0<sigma<s, a subsequence converges strongly in L^p([0,b];dot H^sigma), 1<p<infinity, and weak-star in L-infinity dot H^s to a weak solution with the same bound and L2 conservation a.e.. This solution is unique and C([0,b];dot H^s), with Lipschitz continuous dependence in dot H^s, and conserves L2 at every time: for s>1/2 by the regular-solution uniqueness theorem, for 0<s<=1/2 by the positive rough-solution uniqueness theorem. For s=0 there is likewise a unique C([0,b];L2) weak solution with Lipschitz dependence. For any theta in (-1,0], and any two flows with ||z0||_2+||w0||_2<=B0, sup_{[0,b]}||z-w||_{dot H^theta}<=C' C_{B0}^b ||z0-w0||_{dot H^theta}, where C',C_{B0} depend only on B0,theta.
